files.item: Remembering The Real WWI summer 2016 event series programme.
files.notes: This was the printed programme for the Remembering The Real WWI summer 2016 event series. Featuring Alfred Leete's (1882–1933) Kitchener poster first published as London Opinion, 1914. The photograph of the conscientious objectors was taken at Dyce Camp, near Aberdeen, in September 1916. The silhouette is an adaptation of a still from the film Battle of the Somme, directed by Geoffrey Malins (1886&1940), 1916.

files.item: The printed programme from the Walter Ayles trial play.
files.notes: Walter Ayles was an MP and conscientious objector. This play re-enacted Ayle's appearance before a Military Service Tribunal in the same room where it had taken place 100 years before.

files.item: The printed programme for Remembering The Real WWI autumn 2016 event series.
files.notes: Featuring an illustration by Ralph Chaplin (1887–1961) which was made to support imprisoned members of the Industrial Workers of the World (IWW) during World War I, from Solidarity, 1st September 1917. The silhouette of soldiers if taken from a photograph, 'Infantry moving forward to take over the front line at evening', by Frank Hurley (1885–1962), taken during the Third Battle of Ypres, 1917.

This poster was laid, along with a wreath, in Dings Park to commemorate the deaths of Arthur and Alfred Jefferies during the Somme campaign of 1916. The photograph is from the report of Jeffries death, Western Daily Press, 16th November 1916.

This flyer advertised the commemoration of deaths of Arthur and Alfred Jefferies during the Somme campaign of 1916. The photograph is from the report of Alfred Jeffries death, Western Daily Press, 16th November 1916. The silhouette of soldiers if taken from a photograph, 'Infantry moving forward to take over the front line at evening', by Frank Hurley, taken during the Third Battle of Ypres.

files.item: The printed programme from the Alfred Jeffries walk, 1<sup>st</sup> November 2016.
files.notes: Alfred Jeffries was a conscientious objector from the St Phillips area of Bristol. The walk took place on the centenary of his execution. The photograph is from the report of Jeffries death, Western Daily Press, 16th November 1916.
The design is in the style of the opening credits from Dad's Army, and reflects the pun of the events name.
